findings.headline: Global easing cycle underway; Fed funds midpoint 3.63% (Jun-2026), which sets the backdrop against which Egypt's own 19.00% policy rate normalises
findings.source_name: US Federal Reserve, Federal Open Market Committee policy decisions and the published target range history
findings.model_impact: Anchors the terminal risk-free rate build and the direction of the Kd glide: a falling global rate path is a necessary (not sufficient) condition for the EGP cost-of-debt path assumed in the WACC glide.

findings.headline: Cement is an energy-conversion business: coal/petcoke and electricity are the dominant cash cost. Egypt's phased energy-subsidy reform keeps raising the local energy bill independent of the global fuel price
findings.source_name: Egypt Cement Industry Market Size & Forecast Report 2020-2029 (production faces pressure from energy reform, currency volatility and raw-material management)
findings.model_impact: Sets the EBITDA-margin glide DOWN from the FY2025 peak: energy reform is a structural cost headwind that does not reverse with the cycle.

findings.headline: Cement is a non-traded-at-distance commodity — bulk sea freight limits the economic export radius, so global demand reaches SCEM only through the Mediterranean/East-African export basin, not through a world price
findings.source_name: Global Cement, Egypt country update

findings.headline: Egyptian cement exports fell ~6% y/y to 18.5Mt in 2025, but the MIX inverted: finished-cement exports +66.6% to 12.5Mt while clinker exports fell ~38%
findings.source_name: Global Cement — Egyptian cement exports decline
findings.model_impact: Supports a higher realised price per tonne than a clinker-weighted mix would give; carried in the realised-price driver rather than as a separate export volume leg.

findings.category: sovereign macro (inflation, policy rate, FX/deval risk)
findings.headline: CBE main operation rate 19.50%, held since 2 Apr 2026. Headline inflation eased to 14.6% in May-2026 (core 13.8%); CBE's own Q4-2026 target is 7% (+/-2pp) and it expects the target to be missed on average in Q4-2026 before declining from Q1-2027
findings.source_name: Central Bank of Egypt — policy rate and Monetary Policy Report Q1-2026; CPI release
findings.model_impact: Explicit-window risk-free rate = 19.50%. Terminal rf is norm-built off the CBE's OWN stated medium-term target (7%) plus the standard EM real-rate convention (~5.5pp) = 12.5% -- never a historical average.

findings.category: sovereign macro (inflation, policy rate, FX/deval risk)
findings.headline: Egypt 5-year CDS ~330bp (May-2026), materially tighter than the 2024 crisis peak
findings.source_name: Egypt 5Y CDS series
findings.model_impact: Netted OUT of the local-currency risk-free rate in the Ke build so the sovereign default premium is not charged twice (protocol Ke item 3), and used as the country ERP add-on.

findings.headline: The Egyptian Competition Authority PERMANENTLY lifted cement production quotas in July 2025 (suspended from May 2025). The quota regime had capped output since 2021
findings.source_name: Egyptian Competition Authority, reported via EnterpriseAM / Global Cement
findings.model_impact: BASE CHANGER. Removes the volume cap that held FY2021-24 utilisation down, and simultaneously removes the price floor the cartel-substitute provided. Drives BOTH the volume-recovery driver UP and the realised- price driver DOWN across the forecast window.

findings.headline: Egypt corporate income tax 22.5%, unchanged
findings.source_name: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries (house Cost-of-Capital reference)

findings.category: fiscal / political events with sector read-through
findings.headline: State-led housing, industrial and transport programmes are the marginal buyer of Egyptian cement; domestic consumption rose 13.4% to 54Mt in 2025 on that programme
findings.source_name: Global Cement — Update on Egypt
findings.model_impact: Sets domestic demand growth in the explicit window; the forecast uses the conservative published 2026 estimate (~1%) rather than the 5-8% optimistic case, and sensitises the difference.

findings.headline: 2025 was the first year since 2008 that Egypt's cement supply-demand gap closed: domestic consumption 54Mt (+13.4% from 47.6Mt), production ~65Mt (+18% from 55Mt), operating utilisation ~98% against a nameplate 76Mt/yr across 46 lines
findings.source_name: Global Cement / cemnet (International Cement Review) — Egypt 2025 production
findings.model_impact: BASE CHANGER. Establishes FY2025 as a CYCLICAL PEAK, not a new plateau. The normalised-earnings lens is anchored on this, and the explicit window glides margin down from the FY2025 peak rather than holding it.

findings.headline: Seven to nine dormant production lines are under study for revival, potentially adding 12.6Mt of supply from 2H 2026 -- ~23% of 2025 domestic consumption, landing INSIDE the explicit forecast window
findings.source_name: Global Cement — Update on Egypt
findings.model_impact: The single largest downside driver. Sets the realised-price decline in FY2027-28 and is the mechanism behind the bear case in the sensitivity grid; also caps the terminal margin.

findings.headline: Egyptian cement prices roughly doubled to ~USD 81/t (EGP 3.9k) in 2025 from ~USD 50/t (EGP 2.1k) a year earlier, then are estimated to normalise to EGP 3,600-3,620/t in 2026e on ~1% higher demand and higher costs
findings.source_name: EnterpriseAM Egypt — how Egypt's cement industry fared in 2025 and what's next
findings.model_impact: DRIVER UNLOCK: converts revenue from a top-down growth rate to a bottom-up volume x realised-price unit build. Sets the FY2026 price level directly and the decay path thereafter.

findings.headline: No material substitution threat to Portland cement in Egyptian construction over the forecast horizon; the live technology question is decarbonisation capex (alternative fuels, clinker factor), which is a cost/capex item rather than a demand substitution
findings.source_name: Global Cement sector coverage

findings.headline: Named listed EGX peers all posted the same 2025 step-change: Misr Beni Suef (MBSC) attributable profit +373.7% to EGP 3.946bn on sales of EGP 5.700bn, EPS EGP 61.25, trailing P/E 6.44 and EV/EBITDA 5.03 on a EGP 13.73bn market cap; Arabian Cement (ARCC) FY2025 consolidated profit ~EGP 3.6bn (H1-2025 alone +305.5% to EGP 1.405bn)
findings.source_name: Arab Finance / EGX filings for MBSC and ARCC
findings.model_impact: Sets the relative-multiple lens peer set and confirms the sector-wide (not company-specific) character of the 2025 earnings peak -- which is why the multiple lens is applied to NORMALISED, not trailing, earnings.

findings.headline: SCEM sold its 25.40% stake in Sinai White Portland Cement to Aalborg Portland Holding (Cementir) for EUR 30m; completed 13 Aug 2024, taking Cementir to 96.5% of SWCC
findings.source_name: Cementir Holding N.V. corporate announcement; cemnet/ICR
findings.model_impact: BASE CHANGER, and the key to the whole history. The FY2024 disposal gain is why FY2024 net profit (EGP 3.07bn) is 48% of revenue and why FY2025 profit 'fell' 25% on a 41% revenue rise. FY2024 is excluded as a normalisation base; the gain is stripped to derive underlying FY2024. It also removes the ONLY non-cement earning leg, which is what makes the single operating-company lens correct rather than a two-leg sum.

findings.headline: Vicat, via Vicat Egypt Cement Industries, holds 77.6%; in Jul-2025 it filed a mandatory tender offer for the remaining 58,416,664 shares (22.4%) at EGP 41.00/share
findings.source_name: FRA filing reported via Reuters/TradingView; Vicat H1-2025 results
findings.model_impact: Fixes the free float at 22.4% and the share count at 260,788,678 by back-solving the offer (cross-checked against issued capital). The EGP 41 offer price is a disclosed reference point far BELOW the EGP 79.00 spot and is reported as an overhang, never as a fair value.

findings.headline: Feb-2024 EGM raised authorised capital to EGP 10bn and issued capital by EGP 1.68bn; 168.20m shares offered, 75.95% (127.74m) taken up by senior shareholders in phase 1. Issued capital now EGP 2,608,124,770 at EGP 10 par = 260,812,477 shares
findings.source_name: Sinai Cement EGM resolutions and capital-increase announcements via EGX
findings.model_impact: DRIVER UNLOCK: resolves the share count, which three aggregators report wrongly at 141.46m. Also explains the IAS-33 restatement of FY2023 EPS to -0.88 (unrestated -1.31 on the pre-issue 92.61m shares).

findings.headline: FY2023-FY2025 consolidated: revenue EGP 4.28bn / 6.42bn / 9.09bn; net profit after tax EGP -121.4m / +3,070m / +2,290m; FY2024 EPS attributable EGP 23.13 (FY2023 -0.88 restated); 9M-2025 net profit EGP 1.53bn
findings.source_name: EGX filings reported by Global Cement, cemnet/ICR, Daily News Egypt and Arab Finance
findings.detail: PRIMARY SOURCE NOT RETRIEVABLE: the audited statements at sinaicement.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/SCC-AFS-E-1224.pdf were refused by this environment's egress policy. Provenance is press reporting of the company's own EGX filing, one step removed from the audited print.
findings.model_impact: The disclosed history the model is built on. Revenue and net profit are carried as printed; every line between them is DERIVED and labelled.

findings.headline: Balance sheet: FY2024 total assets EGP 6,385.9m against total liabilities EGP 1,610.9m (equity EGP 4,775.1m -- the triple closes exactly). Latest reported total debt EGP 36.8m against ~EGP 5.2bn equity, i.e. debt/equity 0.7% and a NET CASH position
findings.source_name: EGX filings via aggregated financial summaries
findings.model_impact: Fixes the capital structure: net cash, so the WACC is ~all-equity and the EV->equity bridge ADDS net cash. Treasury income is excluded from FCFF to avoid double-counting the cash.

findings.headline: SCEM operates two lines at El Hassana, North Sinai, ~3.8Mt/yr cement capacity, and reported lifting its market share to ~5% of the Egyptian market
findings.source_name: Company profile and FY2024 results commentary via Daily News Egypt / Global Energy Monitor plant register

findings.headline: Negative search — nothing found (sinaicement.com investor relations, EGX disclosure portal, earnings-call transcripts and results presentations for FY2024/FY2025 -- every host refused by egress policy; no transcript or presentation obtainable from search either)
findings.source_name: negative search

drivers.justification: Built from nameplate capacity (~3.8Mt/yr, two lines) times a utilisation path, cross-checked against the disclosed ~5% share of a 54Mt domestic market, and tied back to disclosed revenue. Quota removal is the unlock that lets utilisation rise.

Disclosed industry price levels (EGP 2.1k 2024 -> 3.9k 2025 -> 3.6k 2026e) give a direct price path; the company's own realised price is solved from disclosed revenue divided by the derived volume, so the build ties back to the printed top line.

Glides down from the FY2025 cyclical peak on two named, dated mechanisms: 12.6Mt of dormant capacity under revival from 2H-2026, and phased energy-subsidy reform, anchored on the disclosed FY2023-25 revenue and profit history.

drivers.driver: Cost of debt (Kd) and the WACC glide
drivers.justification: The company is net cash with EGP 36.8m of gross debt, so Kd carries almost no weight; the glide shape is inherited from the CBE easing path rather than invented.
Norm-built from the CBE's own published medium-term inflation target plus a standard EM real-rate convention, never backed out of a price or averaged from history.

Modelled top-down as a yield on the modelled cash balance. The interest-income line itself is not separately disclosed in any retrievable source, so it cannot be built bottom-up; it is excluded from FCFF entirely and handled in the equity bridge.

No capital-expenditure guidance, maintenance-capex disclosure or investment plan is obtainable; capex is set as a percentage of revenue benchmarked to a mature, fully built two-line plant, and sensitised.
